subject: Field removal windows & obfuscation playbook for EU health insurer
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@eu-insure.io>

Cc: Marco Bianchi <m.bianchi@eu-insure.io>
Date: 2028-04-12T09:15:00Z
Subject: Retention windows + redaction options for our PHI flows

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo earlier today — helpful to see how Redwood routes and caches. We need to align on two things for our procurement/security review:

1) Maximum retention window Redwood would require for request/response logs and cached prefixes when we run models in your EU private deployment. We are constrained by our national regulator to a 30-day default for identifiers unless explicit business justification is recorded.

2) Practical redaction/obfuscation options for PHI fields (names, identifiers, free-text clinical notes). We need choices that balance forensic traceability with regulator expectations (i.e., reversible pseudonymization only with strong controls).

Can you share a short set of options (recommended default + stricter alternatives) and the operational implications (backup retention, audit logs, reconstitution risk)? Attaching the sections from our security questionnaire for context.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of IT Security
EU HealthInsure SA

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-04-12T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention windows + redaction options for our PHI flows

Elena —

Appreciate the notes and the questionnaire excerpt. High-level answers below; I pulled in Lauren and Markus because there are product and threat-model tradeoffs.

Short answers (we can expand into a one-pager):
- Retention: default TTL for request/response logs in private deployments is configurable by you; our default hosted policy is 90 days, but for Private we support configurable windows down to 0 days (ephemeral) subject to audit/backup constraints. For EU-regulated installs we commonly set 30 days for logs and 7 days for KV/prefix caches.
- Redaction/obfuscation options we support: (A) Non-reversible field-level removal at ingest (recommended for strict compliance), (B) Deterministic pseudonymization (reversible only with customer-managed KMS keys and RBAC), (C) Tokenization with split keys (best for forensic reconstitution but operationally heavier).

Operational implications: backup retention may require preserving metadata for up to your retention window; if you choose reversible pseudonymization we need KMS integration and strict key rotation policies. Markus, can you confirm the default audit/log footprint for Private?

I attached a brief matrix (redaction-options-playbook.pdf) with recommended defaults. Happy to jump on a short call to run through specifics.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Retention windows + redaction options for our PHI flows

Quick technical add:

- For Private deployments (VPC), logs are stored in an encrypted object store controlled by the customer. We can configure lifecycle policies to expire objects after N days — N is set per-tenant. That covers request/response storage.
- Prefix/KV caches used for performance are normally in-memory on serving nodes; we persist minimal metadata to object storage for warm-starts. If the customer requires zero persistence, we can disable warm-starts and set caches to ephemeral-only (tradeoff: cold-start latency).
- Reversible pseudonymization: implemented as AES-GCM envelope encryption where the DEK is encrypted by the customer's KMS. Redwood never stores the unwrapped DEK. Reconstitution requires KMS unwrap permissions.
- Non-reversible redaction: we apply field scrubbing at the ingestion layer, remove PII/PHI tokens, and write a redaction marker. No keys needed; cannot reconstitute.

I recommend Elena's team pick: (1) field deletion for identifiers + (2) deterministic pseudonymization for non-identifier context fields where you need analytics linkage. That gives a defensible posture with limited reconstitution risk.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@eu-insure.io>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention windows + redaction options for our PHI flows

Elena —

Summarizing proposed default configuration for your procurement checklist (we can encode these as profile templates in Private):

- Logs (audit + request/response): 30-day TTL (object lifecycle). Longer retention only with signed business justification.
- Prefix/KV caches: 7-day TTL by default; option to set ephemeral-only to meet strict regulator asks.
- Field handling policy (default profile):
  * Identifiers (SSNs, national IDs): ingest-level deletion (irreversible).
  * Names & direct identifiers: deterministic pseudonymization using customer KMS (allow re-id by ops with KMS unwrap audit).
  * Free-text clinical notes: configurable; default is retain redacted excerpt (first 200 chars masked) + secure hashed pointer for duplicate detection.

Next steps: 1) confirm whether EU HealthInsure requires ephemeral caches (i.e., no persisted KV) and 2) whether legal will allow reversible pseudonymization under KMS control. Once confirmed, we will produce contract clause language and slide into the SOW.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director of Product, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Retention windows + redaction options for our PHI flows

Team —

Thanks, this is exactly the level of granularity we needed. Two quick decisions from our side after internal review:

1) We will require ephemeral-only prefix caches for the first 12 months of the pilot (so no persisted KV warm-starts). Please confirm expected cold-start penalty and mitigation options.

2) For identifiers and direct PII we confirm ingest-level deletion. For names and other linking attributes we will proceed with deterministic pseudonymization tied to our KMS (we will provide access controls and rotation schedule).

Action items:
- Marco and I will send the legal redlines for the SOW by Friday — please prepare a short contract addendum for reversible pseudonymization/KMS obligations.
- Can Redwood provide a short note on incident response implications when KMS unwraps are required for reconstitution? We need audit-ready language.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena
Head of IT Security, EU HealthInsure SA
